📖 How to Play & Updates

📌 Current build reference — v175.4.4
This guide has been audited against the current game code. Older update notes remain historical; when an old note conflicts with this current-build reference, the current-build section is authoritative.
⌨️ Core controls
W A S D — move Space — jump; hold against a solid wall to climb Ctrl — sprint while held (or use the sprint-toggle setting) Shift — dive/swim down; also used by stack-drop and quiver unload LMB — mine, attack, knap, draw/release bow depending on context RMB — place/interact with held blocks and physical crafting actions E — eat/drink or retrieve a ready cooking-pot meal; opens Creative Inventory in Creative Q — drop held item; Shift+Q can drop the whole stack when enabled R — rotate held blocks and several context craft/carve actions; nock arrow with bow F — forage, fish, butcher, read tracks, mount/dismount raft depending on context X — physical crafting/assembly trigger for many tools, materials and structures B — bandage/medical context and fire-fanning/cooking heat interaction G — fan/blow fire and toggle Blueprint Grid mode V — Pickup (default). Hold nothing and look AT a water block + V to drink. Hold a Canteen (Shell) or filled Clay Pot + V to drink from that container. Otherwise V picks up the nearest dropped item. Z — sleep when a usable bed is nearby C — cooking-pot context action (water/ingredient interaction) P — physical cooking preparation of the last ingredient when the cooking interaction is available L — load quiver; Shift+L unloads quiver H — equip/unequip backpack O — open Separate Bag backpack storage K — Knowledge / skill mastery panel Tab — stats / player list depending on multiplayer state M — fullscreen world map N — night vision J — in-game How-to-Play book F2 — screenshot / — debug information overlay Alt — release the mouse without opening the pause menu; press/click again to re-lock Esc — pause/settings interface
🎯 How to start survival play
1. Get food. Forage berries/fruit, hunt animals, fish, or gather roots. Keep some quick food while you establish a camp.
2. Get basic materials. Wood, sticks, flint, leaves/vines, stone and clay are the main early material families.
3. Get safe water. The world contains fresh, salt and dirty water states; water quality matters later for cooking and disease.
4. Make shelter/fire. Weather, temperature, darkness and fatigue become important once you stay out longer.
5. Build tools physically. This game emphasizes repeated world actions rather than a single crafting menu.
6. Explore outward. The world is chunk-streamed procedural terrain. New chunks can contain geology, caves, plants, animals, water and structures/features.
🧭 World interaction rules
• Blocks are stored in a persistent world registry and edited blocks are recorded as chunk modifications.
• Building/breaking can trigger local terrain/mesh rebuilds, plant/prop updates, water reflow and map invalidation.
• Dropped items have physics, can be picked up automatically or manually, and many compatible items can merge into piles.
• The game keeps player state, world edits and many settings across sessions.
• Multiplayer shares player positions and many world interactions through the room connection.
🗺 Map & information
M opens the fullscreen map. It is generated from the game's procedural terrain functions rather than a separate fake world image.
The map uses terrain height, biome and the current surface resolver. Environmental water is based on procedural terrain/sea level, while transient flowing-water particles are not treated as permanent lakes.
Settings → Map Settings provides Minimap ON/OFF, Fast / Smart / Low Power updates, Close / Normal / Wide range, grid toggle, player/animal display toggles, and fullscreen zoom.
Map samples are cached and invalidated when terrain/world changes, so moving is the main normal refresh trigger and edits can force a refresh.
⚙️ Settings that matter during normal play
FOV: 60°, 75°, 90°, 100°, 110°.
Render distance: Far / Normal / Near / Very Near; the live chunk streamer also adapts render distance when FPS drops.
Simulation distance (v175.4.4): Short (48) / Normal (96) / Far (160) / Very Far (240) blocks. Controls how far animal AI, farming, and other simulation systems actively run. Independent from render distance — you can see far without simulating far.
Day speed: Very Fast (15 min), Fast (30 min), Normal (60 min), Slow (120 min) per full day/night cycle.
Difficulty: Peaceful / Easy / Normal / Hard. Peaceful removes survival drain and aggressive-animal pressure; higher modes increase survival/damage pressure.
Accessibility: font scale, colorblind presentation (6 modes: Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia, Achromatopsia, High Contrast), audio subtitles, text-to-speech, visual sound cues, and reduced-motion options are persisted.
🌱 Farming genetics (v175.4.4)
Seeds carry 5 genetic traits that are inherited by offspring with small mutations:
• Growth Rate — how fast the plant progresses through stages.
• Yield — base harvest quantity.
• Size — affects harvest output (yield × size) and water demand. Larger plants use slightly more water.
• Drought Resistance — plants below 35% moisture get a growth penalty; high drought resistance reduces that penalty. Also reduces moisture loss rate.
• Cold Resistance — winter applies a stronger growth penalty to crops with poor cold resistance. Autumn gets a smaller effect. High cold resistance reduces the slowdown.
Harvest = yield × size. A high-yield/high-size plant produces more than a low-yield/small plant. Same applies to berry bushes and fruit trees.
Breed better crops by harvesting plants with desirable traits and replanting their genetically-inherited seeds over multiple generations.
🍲 Physical cooking — no fixed recipe list
Cooking is player-made. You do not choose a premade recipe. The game builds the result from the ingredients you actually add, their preparation state, water type, fire heat and cooking progress.
Cooking Pot: make the pot through the physical clay/coiling and firing process, place it in the world, then fill it with a fresh, salt or dirty water source using the Clay Pot interaction.
Ingredients: the current pot accepts up to four cookable inputs. Current inputs include raw meat, dried meat, berries/bush berries, fruit and roots.
Preparation: with a knife, use P near the filled pot to prepare the most recently added ingredient. The current implementation supports a first cut/chop and then a finer preparation step; preparation feeds the emergent quality model.
Fire distance: the pot only cooks while it is within roughly 4 blocks of a campfire. The game uses the nearest fire's heat state and a spatial lookup rather than checking every fire.
Heat: the fire has multiple heat tiers. Higher heat advances cooking faster, but it also reaches the burn threshold sooner.
B — blow on the fire: standing near a campfire and pressing B raises its heat, adds a small amount of fuel time and updates nearby cooking speed. It also costs a small amount of hunger.
🧪 What determines the meal
The emergent food model tracks ingredient contributions such as protein, fat, carbohydrates, vitamins, fiber, hydration and flavor, plus preparation quality, heat and cooking progress.
More ingredients can improve the combined nutrition profile, while preparation changes the quality contribution of the prepared ingredient.
The final meal name is generated from what you actually made rather than selected from a fixed recipe table.
Fresh water: the clean baseline and gives a small health benefit.
Salt water: extends preservation but slightly lowers the health benefit.
Dirty water: reduces benefits and adds a strong contamination/dysentery risk.
⏱️ Timing: undercook → good → burn
Under-cooked: removing food too early produces a lower-quality result with additional sickness risk.
Good/browned window: cooking through the intended window gives the strongest thermal quality and can produce a browned result.
Overcooked: quality drops as cooking continues beyond the ideal window.
Burned: crossing the burn threshold creates a burned food state. Burned food has poor nutrition and can hurt/sicken the player.
The pot can visually change as it progresses, and the game warns when the food is ready and when it is approaching or has crossed the burn point.
🔥 Cooking Spit — one item, direct roasting
Craft: Stick + Rope.
Use: place the spit beside a campfire, hold raw meat and press C to skewer it.
The spit uses the nearby fire's heat to advance roast progress. At the normal roast point it produces cooked meat; leave it on the heat too long and it produces Charred Meat.
The spit is intentionally not a recipe machine. It is a physical single-item roasting process that complements the multi-ingredient Cooking Pot.
🌧️ Rain Collector — build your own water source
Craft: Plank + Rope + Cloth.
Place: put it under open sky. It stores fresh rainwater while rain is active.
Collect: use an empty Clay Pot with C nearby to take the stored fresh water.
This creates a physical survival loop: build the collector, wait for weather, then move the collected water into your cooking/drinking setup.
💡 Cooking strategy
There is no single “best recipe.” Experiment with different ingredients, preparation levels, water sources and fire temperatures.
Use lower heat when you want more control over timing. Use higher heat when you need food faster and can watch it closely.
Keep the fire fed, because moving the cooking process outside the useful heat range stops progress.
For exact current behavior, the game runtime is authoritative; this tab is a player-facing guide to the physical systems rather than a recipe database.
❤️ Survival model
Health: the player has a 100-point health pool. Damage can come from falls, combat, bleeding, cold/wet exposure, fire and disease. A global damage cap limits certain simultaneous drain stacks.
Hunger: base drain is 0.3 per second. Extreme hunger can become direct HP loss. Sprinting increases food demand.
Thirst: base drain is 0.45 per second. Water quality and environment affect safe hydration.
Calories: a longer-term energy reserve used by fatigue/recovery systems.
Fatigue: sustained sprinting, climbing and physical crafting consume it. Sleep is the main recovery action.
Temperature: season, altitude, wind, rain, shelter, wetness, biome and fires affect body temperature.
🌡️ Exposure, weather & shelter
Weather includes changing wind, gusts, rain and storms. Visual weather effects, audio, animal behavior and player/environment calculations are separate systems but respond to the same weather state.
Wetness makes cold exposure worse. Fire provides warmth, but fire also creates burn risk when you stand too close.
Shelter reduces wind exposure. The game periodically samples shelter around the player rather than recomputing the expensive scan every frame.
Tornadoes can appear as world events; wind also affects trees, particles, rafts and loose objects.
🩸 Wounds & disease
Bleeding: can follow combat/animal injury and should be treated promptly.
Wound infection / sepsis: persistent infection can progress into severe HP drain.
Flu/cold exposure: prolonged wet/cold conditions can trigger illness and worsen movement/survival pressure.
Dysentery: dirty-water use/cooking can create contamination risk.
Frostbite: extreme cold exposure can progress into serious injury.
Tetanus: deep animal bites can trigger it; Antiseptic Moss is the targeted remedy.
Scurvy: prolonged lack of fruit/berries can trigger it; fruit/berry consumption helps recover.
Herbal remedies and food effects are integrated into the disease system rather than being purely cosmetic status messages.
🔥 Fire & campfire survival
Campfires are physical world objects with a fuel timer, flame mesh, smoke, light and heat state.
Fuel can be fed by compatible loose materials. Fires can spread to flammable world blocks and can generate wind-blown embers.
B near a fire: fans the flame, increases heat, adds a small amount of fuel time and accelerates cooking. Blowing also consumes a small amount of hunger.
Rain can suppress/kill fire and embers. Fires provide warmth but can damage the player at very close range.
🍲 Current v98 cooking: no recipe book
Step 1 — make a Cooking Pot: form the clay pot through the physical clay-coiling system, then fire it to obtain the Cooking Pot.
Step 2 — fill water: use a filled Clay Pot near the cooking fire and press C. The cooking pot stores fresh, salt or dirty water.
Step 3 — choose ingredients: add up to 4 cookable ingredients. Current cookable inputs are raw meat, dried meat, berries, wild/bush berries, fruit and roots.
Step 4 — prepare: hold a knife and use P on the filled pot. The latest ingredient can be cut/chopped and then finely prepared. Preparation changes the emergent food profile instead of selecting a recipe.
Step 5 — cook: the pot cooks only while within about 4 blocks of a campfire. Fire heat determines the real-time cooking speed.
Step 6 — retrieve: once the pot is ready, press E near it. The game creates an emergent food result from ingredients, preparation, water, heat and timing.
There is deliberately no fixed recipe table. The result can be named things such as a cooked single ingredient, a mixed pot, a rich/fresh variant, a browned variant, an under-cooked variant, salted, or contaminated based on what you actually did.
Too little cooking: under-cooked food has a sickness penalty/risk.
Good timing: the cooking window produces the highest thermal quality and can produce a browned result.
Too much cooking: after the burn threshold the meal becomes burned, has poor nutrition and can hurt/sicken the player.
Water effects: salt water preserves longer but slightly lowers health benefit; dirty water adds a large dysentery risk and reduces health benefit; fresh water is the clean baseline.
Emergent nutrition: the current model tracks protein, fat, carbs, vitamins, fiber, hydration, flavor, heat, cooking progress and preparation quality internally, then derives hunger/health/spoil effects.
Cooking Spit: a player-made single-item roasting tool. Craft it from Stick + Rope, place it beside a fire, hold raw meat and press C to skewer the meat. Fire heat drives roast speed; the item becomes cooked first and can become Charred Meat if left cooking too long.
Rain Collector: a player-made water tool built from Plank + Rope + Cloth. Place it under open sky. During rain it slowly stores fresh rainwater; use an empty Clay Pot with C nearby to collect the stored water.
🏺 Drinking straight from a Clay Pot (raw water)
Hold a filled Clay Pot and press V to drink it raw, skipping the Cooking Pot entirely. It's faster, but only boiled water is guaranteed safe — raw water gambles on bacteria.
Fresh water (raw): +35 thirst, only a small (~4%) chance of a mild dysentery bout.
Dirty water (raw): +18 thirst, but a high (~30%) chance of dysentery, and more severe when it hits.
Salt water (raw): always a bad idea — costs 15 thirst instead of restoring it, with no upside. Never drink salt water raw.
Boiled Water (Cooking Pot, then E): the only 100% safe option — +55 thirst, +6 HP, zero infection risk. Costs time and fuel instead of health risk.
Either way, the Clay Pot empties after drinking and can be refilled immediately at any water source (C key).
Rule of thumb: raw fresh water is a reasonable gamble when you're desperate and near clean water; raw dirty water almost never is — boil it instead if you have the time.
🌾 Farming
Grass/dirt can be tilled into farmland when suitable water is nearby.
Seeds are planted onto farmland, then progress through seedling → growing → mature stages.
Growth is faster near water and varies by season: spring faster, autumn slower, winter much slower.
Harvest/regrowth systems integrate with the same world registry and saved chunk modifications used by normal building.
⚒ Physical crafting philosophy
This game intentionally mixes direct crafting actions with inventory assembly. Important early actions are physical: flint striking, rope twisting, clay coiling, fire making, wood splitting and butchering.
Knowledge is earned by doing. The K panel tracks Knapping, Cordage, Firecraft, Carpentry and Hunting mastery. Crafting quality comes from the physical work you perform; the character does not gain a crafting level that replaces the work.
Many crafted results still use X as the final assembly trigger; the required materials and physical setup are part of the world rather than a recipe-screen selection.
🪨 Flint & stone tools
Flint nodes are geological world objects. Early progression uses flint to make a cutting edge, then combine that with other simple materials for weapons and tools.
The physical knapping system uses repeated strikes and angle/context rather than a single instant recipe.
Spears can be used in melee and as thrown projectiles; the projectile is simulated separately from the melee hit.
🪢 Cordage, wood & hide
Cordage: plant fibre/vines are processed and twisted through a physical action. Wet/damaged fibre can affect the result.
Wood: logs can be split into planks and sticks; wood actions also feed bow, raft, building and structural crafting.
Hide: animal carcasses support multi-step butchering and yield species-dependent materials such as hide, bone, meat and tallow.
Clay: multiple clay qualities exist. Refining/washing clay before coiling is safer; pure clay is the reliable pot-making material.
🔥 Firecraft & fuel
Early fire starts from an ember + nearby fuel. Rain can kill an exposed ember. Once lit, the campfire becomes a persistent physical system.
Fire also feeds cooking, warmth, clay firing, metal processing and some other survival actions. It can spread and generate embers.
🏹 Bow & arrow system
Bow use is draw-based: hold the attack action to build draw strength, then release to fire. Arrows are consumed.
The current game supports multiple arrow types, including base/flint, fire, feathered, heavy, poison and obsidian variants.
Fire arrows must be ignited near a real campfire/fire before shooting. Other arrow types modify speed, gravity, damage or effects.
Hit location matters for animal/player damage, and weapon material plus player strength affect the final damage calculation.
⛓️ Iron / advanced metalworking
Advanced progression includes charcoal production, iron ore processing, hot iron bloom/ingot states, anvil shaping and tool assembly.
Hot metal carries a heat value and can be quenched in water. Heat and quenching affect durability/quality of finished tools.
Anvil output is contextual: the block/material setup above the anvil influences which head/weapon form is produced.
Obsidian weapons form a separate high-damage/brittle material tier.
🎒 Backpacks, storage & utility
Backpacks have multiple tiers and can use either Extra Slots mode or Separate Bag storage mode.
In Separate Bag mode, the backpack has its own storage interface and can be opened with O while worn.
Chests provide persistent world storage and are synchronized in multiplayer.
⛵ Build-your-own raft / ship system
There is no fixed boat mesh you must use. Connected floating blocks become a raft/ship when the game scans them as a connected group of at least 2 blocks.
Buoyancy is calculated from the block group's mass/volume and the current water surface. The craft can sink if it is too heavy for its displaced volume.
Asymmetric block placement changes center-of-mass / center-of-buoyancy and produces roll/pitch. The craft can tilt rather than staying perfectly level.
Water, wind and current all affect movement. Wake particles appear when moving fast enough.
🧱 Construction
Use floating wood/hull-compatible blocks as the core. Connect them physically in the world; the raft scanner groups touching float-capable blocks.
Rudder improves turning.
Keel reduces drift and reduces tilt response.
Mast + sail gives wind propulsion in favorable wind direction.
Heavier materials increase mass and can reduce maximum practical speed or make a craft sink.
🎮 Sailing
Walk within boarding range and press F to mount. Press F again to dismount.
W/S paddle/drive forward or backward while riding.
A/D turn. Rudders multiply turning authority.
Shift provides a temporary faster paddle/throttle multiplier.
A mast/sail increases forward force when the wind is aligned with the craft. Keel count reduces current drift.
If the raft group breaks below the minimum connected block count, the raft can disappear as a valid craft and the rider is safely displaced beside it.
🌍 Procedural world
The world is infinite-style, chunked procedural terrain. Chunks are 16×16 in X/Z and are streamed around the player.
Terrain height is generated from deterministic seeded noise with broad continental shaping, fine detail and coast/erosion shaping. The same deterministic functions drive the new map.
World vertical limits include bedrock around Y = −38. Sea level/water base is Y = 2.
Underground generation includes sediment/geology layers, caves, ore/mineral deposits, clay, salt and volcanic/deep-world features depending on world type.
New chunks can require more work the first time they are streamed, but generation is budgeted and worker-assisted to keep frame spikes manageable.
🌊 Water
Water has a base sea-level plane. The water simulation also supports flowing/spreading water blocks.
Dynamic flow water is gameplay state and is intentionally different from the permanent environmental water used by the map.
Swimming uses buoyancy/drag, oxygen and current effects. Deep ocean water can create noticeable current force.
Water quality is classified into fresh, salt and dirty states for drinking/cooking systems.
🌿 Flora & agriculture
Natural generation includes trees, leaves, vines, resin, bushes, berries, fruit trees and aquatic/coastal vegetation.
Berry bushes are persistent world props and use internal cooldown/regrowth rather than spawning a replacement block above them after harvest.
Farming is world-based: till actual terrain, plant a seed block, let it progress through growth stages, then harvest.
🐾 Animals
Animals are simulated as living world entities with species data, health, attack behavior, predator/prey logic, energy and movement.
Species can migrate seasonally; fresh tracks can help you follow herds.
Weather affects animal activity, movement and survival. Winter, rain, storms and wind each modify behavior/spawn pressure.
Predators can hunt prey and some species defend territory. Bears can hibernate, while herd species use group behavior.
🌪️ Weather, seasons & sky
Day/night is continuous and configurable in Settings. The default full cycle is 300 seconds.
Wind can change direction, produce gusts and influence trees, loose particles, rafts and some player/environment forces.
Rain changes visibility, wetness, fire behavior and temperature. Seasonal overlays include frost, aurora/rainbow and snow/cold effects depending on conditions.
Tornadoes are active world events that influence weather/audio/particles and player danger.
🗺️ Map accuracy model
The rebuilt map samples the same procedural groundH/biomeAt system as world generation and consults the surface resolver when available.
It derives hill shading from neighboring terrain heights.
Environmental water is considered water when the procedural surface is at/below the water level; transient flowing-water particle state is not drawn as fake permanent lakes.
Map samples are cached and invalidated after world/terrain edits and water-changing events.
🐾 Animals — Behavior & Interaction
v175.4 includes a deep animal system with genetics, age, neural recognition, physical marking, and carry mechanics.
👁 Observing Animals
• Press Y to open the Animal Behavior Panel.
• Look at an animal + click 📌 to pin it.
• 5 tabs: Traits (genetics + vitals) · Recognize (trust scores) · Tags (learned tag meanings) · Log (observation history) · Animals (full world list with teleport).
• Press Esc → 🧠 Neural Debug for live activity overlay.
📊 Animal Traits (Genetics)
Each animal has 7 general traits + 3-5 species-specific traits:
General: Vitality (HP), Fertility (breeding), Longevity (lifespan), Metabolism (hunger), Temperament (aggression), Intelligence (learning speed), Constitution (stamina/carry).
Species: e.g. Wolf has Pack Coordination, Prey Drive, Territory, Howl Range. Cow has Milk Yield, Docility, Girth, Heat Tolerance.
Traits are inherited from parents with small mutations. Breed animals with high-value traits over generations to improve your herd.
🔄 Life Stages
Baby (0-1 day) → Juvenile (1-3) → Adult (3-25) → Senior → Death
Seniors get silver fur and produce higher-quality hides but have reduced fertility. Animals die naturally of old age. Longevity trait extends adult stage.
🧠 Recognition & Trust
Animals watch you and learn. Each animal builds a trust score (-1.0 to +1.0) based on:
• Feeding (+) · Attacking (-) · Killing (-) · Building (+)
• Passive proximity (+) · Watching PvP combat (+/-)

Trust levels:
Bonded (>+0.5) — follows you, defends you
Tamed (>+0.2) — doesn't flee, tolerates proximity
Neutral — species default behavior
Wary (<-0.2) — flees at extended range
Hostile (<-0.5) — predators attack, prey panics

Tags (e.g., @rancher) are Bayesian priors — animals learn what tags mean by observing behavior. A @raider who kills livestock teaches all nearby animals to distrust the @raider tag.
🏷 Marking Animals — Physical Crafting
Marked animals show on minimap, get a floating name tag in the world, and persist across saves and multiplayer.
🔥 IRON BRAND — reusable, carve once + reheat per use
1. Smelt iron ore → bloom (existing system)
2. Hold Iron Bloom + look at Anvil + press X repeatedly (~20 strikes) → bloom flattens into brand shape
3. Hold brand-shaped Bloom + have Chisel + look at Anvil + press X → carves a pattern
4. Place Bloom on campfire → heats red-hot
5. Hold heated Bloom + look at animal + press E → imprints pattern
6. Bloom cools. Reheat to brand again. Same pattern every time.
👤 LEATHER COLLAR — 1 use, cut from hide directly
1. Butcher animal → Hide Piece drops → place it as a block on ground
2. Hold Sharp Flint + look at placed Hide Piece + press R → carve strip shape
3. Hold carved Hide Piece + press X to grab end → pull → Leather Strip in inventory
4. Hold Leather Strip + have Sharp Flint + press R → punches 1 hole (repeat 3-5x)
5. Hold Leather Strip (holed) + have Rope + press X → Collar Assembled
6. Hold Collar + look at animal + press E → wraps and ties (collar consumed)
🎨 PAINT — quantity-based, branch is the brush
1. Make a pot: Clay Pot (fired) / forge Iron Pot / carve Wooden Pot
2. Get pigment: crush berries/fruit/charcoal/ore with Rock or Stick → Pigment block (works indoors or outdoors)
  Red (berries) · Yellow (fruit) · Black (charcoal) · Brown (iron ore) · Green (copper ore) · Gold (gold ore)
3. Fill a Clay Pot with water using C, then place the Clay Pot in the world. The pot is a real volume — its water level matters.
4. Hold Pigment + look at the placed pot + press X → add pigment. Pigment stacks and blends — more pigment = thicker, more opaque paint. Different pigments mix their colors.
5. Hold a Stick + look at the placed pot + press X → stir/mix only. Then press F with the Stick → dip/load the brush (each dip = 5 strokes, uses 5 pigment + 10% of the pot's water).
6. Hold the loaded Stick + LMB on a micro-voxel block → paints surface cells using the Stick brush size. The brush dims as it runs out — dip again to reload. The stick tip shows the paint color.
7. Small tree → 1×1 brush · Medium tree → 3×3 brush · Large tree → 5×5 brush.
8. Paint depletes with use: pigment AND water both run out. Refill water: look at the pot + C near water. Rain slowly washes exposed paint pots (iron-ochre resists best) but refills plain water pots.
8. Hold a loaded Stick + look at an animal + press E → marks animal (lasts 7 days)
✋ Carrying Animals
Press H to pick up small animals or babies of any species.
Your Strength stat determines carry capacity:
• 0.3 strength → 17.5kg max
• 1.0 strength → 35kg max

Carrying slows movement and drains stamina — both scale with strength. Build strength by sprinting, combat, and carrying.
🥛 Animal Products
Cows produce milk (female cows only, milkYield trait affects rate).
Chickens lay eggs (hens only, eggRate trait affects rate).
Press E near a ready cow/chicken to harvest. Milk restores +35 thirst. Eggs can be eaten or cooked.
🐾 Animals Tab — Full World List
The 🐾 Animals tab shows every animal in the world:
• Sort by distance (closest first)
• Filter: All / Marked / Trusted / Hostile / Babies
• Actions per animal: 📌 Pin · 📍 Teleport · 🏷 Mark · ✋ Carry
💪 Strength-Based Combat
Heavy attack (hold LMB >0.5s): 2x damage, 25 stamina, requires str ≥ 0.5
Stamina gates damage: < 10 stamina = 50% damage, no heavy attacks
Weapon strength scaling: Iron Axe 1.5x, Obsidian Sword 1.3x, Fist 0.5x
Build strength by: sprinting, landing melee hits, killing predators, carrying animals, drawing bow to full.
🆕 v99 — Verified Wiki / Current-System Update
The game's single version string is now synchronized to v99. This update refreshes the player wiki from the current runtime behavior instead of relying on historical recipe text.
🍲 v100 → Dedicated Cooking Guide Tab
Added a dedicated Cooking tab to both tutorial views so the physical Cooking Pot, ingredient preparation, heat/timing, Cooking Spit and Rain Collector systems have their own reference page.
🍖 v99 → Player-Made Cooking & Weather Tools
• Cooking Spit: build it from Stick + Rope, place it beside a fire, then use raw meat on it. Fire heat controls roast speed, and leaving it on a hot fire too long can char the meat.
• Rain Collector: build it from Plank + Rope + Cloth, place it under open sky, and collect stored fresh rainwater with an empty Clay Pot during/after rain.
🍲 v97 → v98 Cooking documentation alignment
• Removed the old assumption that meals are selected from a fixed recipe table.
• Documented physical ingredient preparation with a knife and P on the latest ingredient.
• Documented emergent meal profiles built from ingredient properties, preparation, water quality, heat and cooking progress.
• Documented under-cooked / browned / overcooked / burned states and the fact that the game generates the meal name from what the player actually combined.
• Documented multiplayer cooking state as input/preparation/profile data rather than a preset recipe id.
🗺 v95–v96 Map / cooking fixes carried forward
• Map settings are persisted: minimap, update cadence, range, grid, player/animal display and fullscreen zoom.
• Map water classification is based on procedural terrain/sea level rather than stale flowing-water particles, preventing random blue specks/lakes.
• Cooking visual state uses the same dynamic heat-derived cook/burn times as simulation instead of outdated fixed constants.
🫐 v92–v94 stability work
• Berry bushes use a persistent harvest/regrowth state and are protected from the old disappearing-on-neighbor-edit bug.
• Chunk/terrain rebuilding now has recovery protection so transient feature work does not erase a valid terrain mesh.
• Streamed chunks use authoritative base/world edit state before feature decoration.
• The map/fullscreen-map state is separated from the pause menu so M can open the map reliably.
⚙️ Performance architecture currently in the build
• Chunk generation is worker-assisted and can use shared buffers where the browser supports the required isolation settings.
• Main-thread chunk finishing is queued and budgeted instead of performing every expensive stage in a single frame.
• Terrain mesh backing arrays are reused to reduce garbage collection.
• Nearby-fire queries use a spatial grid for cooking instead of pots × all-campfires scanning.
• Entity frustum objects are reused and terrain queries are cached/bounded.
• Adaptive graphics can lower pixel ratio, render distance and shadow quality when FPS falls, with cooldown/hysteresis to avoid rapid quality flapping.
• The minimap uses cached procedural terrain samples and only redraws when movement/terrain invalidation says it needs to.
Historical v1–v95 notes remain in the older changelog for context. They describe when systems were introduced, not necessarily their exact current implementation. Use the Basics / Survival / Crafting / Rafts / World tabs above for the current behavior.
📋 Planned Updates — Roadmap
These are planned directions, not current features. The roadmap may change as systems are tested and optimized.
🧱 1. Micro-Voxel Physical World
Expand the 16×16×16 micro-cell system into the main world for precise carving, sculpting and localized damage. Keep micro-edited blocks localized so normal terrain remains cheap.
Goal: one physical editing system for terrain, wood, stone and manufactured parts.
🌲 2. Realistic Tree Chopping & Woodworking
Axe hits will create localized trunk damage instead of simply deleting a whole wood block. Repeated cuts can create notches, weaken support, disconnect branches and eventually cause the tree to fall through the existing structural system.
Follow-up woodworking is planned around splitting, carving, shaping and joining wood instead of instant log-to-plank conversions.
🔪 3. Physical Butchering
Expand carcasses into localized resource regions so the player's actual processing actions determine what is separated and how cleanly it is recovered. The existing multi-step carcass interaction will remain the foundation.
Planned resource regions include meat, hide, fat, bone and organs, with species and tool differences affecting the result.
🛠️ 4. Player-Skill Crafting — No Crafting Levels
Remove character crafting mastery as a gameplay modifier. Craft quality should come from the player's actions, positioning, timing, material choice, tool condition and the physical state of the object.
Goal: the player gets better at crafting; the character does not gain a hidden crafting level.
⚒️ 5. Replace Remaining Instant Craft Shortcuts
Continue removing obsolete “materials + X = finished object” paths wherever a physical replacement exists. Planned targets include more woodworking, cordage, weapon assembly, containers, forging and arrow construction.
🧵 6. Worker-Driven Simulation & Micro-Meshing
Move expensive micro-mesh generation and other suitable physical-world jobs into the worker/job pipeline, batch edits, reuse buffers and avoid rebuilding whole chunks for tiny changes.
🥊 10. Punch-Based Micro-Voxel Interaction (Planned)
When the player punches (bare-fist LMB) a block, the impact should target the block's micro-voxels — chipping away at the surface shape rather than mining the whole block. If the block is solid (no micro-voxel data yet), the punch picks it up directly (instant break for soft blocks like grass/leaves). This unifies the "punch" and "mine" flows into a single physical interaction: every hit shapes the world at the micro level.
Goal: punching always does something tangible — either carves micro-voxels or picks up the block — instead of the current slow-mining-bar approach.
🏭 7. Realistic Technology Progression
Long-term progression is planned to go beyond the medieval/early-industrial ceiling toward steam, industrial machinery, electricity and advanced engineering while keeping the world grounded in physical technology.
🌍 8. More Interconnected World Systems
Planned systems are intended to feed one another: ecology → hunting → butchering → food/preservation → materials → tools → industry → infrastructure. The goal is fewer isolated mechanics and more consequences flowing through the world.
🌐 9. Browser-First Performance
Keep the game playable directly in the browser while adding depth. Planned work continues on worker scheduling, memory reuse, simulation LOD, micro-detail LOD, multiplayer efficiency and main-thread reduction.
